For vocations, there were only two that overlapped when combining FleetDNA and CE-CERT data: the drayage vocation in the combination-unit short-haul source type and the towing vocation in the single-unit short-haul source type. As there are only two combined vocation graphs, we will show these images in the body of the text rather than in an appendix. 20 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 12 displays the combined FleetDNA and CE-CERT data for the source type combination- unit short-haul data. Compared to the FleetDNA data density for this source type shown in Figure 2, urban freeways on weekends now have double the vehicles and four times the hours and constitute a robust sample (no shading). For weekdays, we have increased our vehicle count and hours recorded in all groups, but rural roads did not gain enough data to cross the near-30 threshold for solid vehicle and hour counts (still shaded yellow). Figure 12. Combined data density for combination-unit short-haul vehicles Figure 13 shows combined FleetDNA and CE-CERT data for single-unit short-haul vehicles. Despite neither data set alone having enough vehicles or hours to be analyzed in this category, rural other roads on weekdays now have eight vehicles and will be shown in the combined analysis going forward. We also gained vehicles and hours for urban driving, and these groups are augmented in confidence while not changing data quality classification (shaded color). 21 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 13. Combined data density for single-unit short-haul vehicles Figure 14 illustrates the data available for refuse trucks from the combined analysis. Due to the CE-CERT data, we can now analyze rural freeway weekday data and urban freeway weekend data. We can also now be more confident in urban freeway driving, which is no longer shaded yellow as the two data sets complemented each other nicely. 22 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 14. Combined data density for refuse trucks Figure 15 displays combined data density for transit buses. Understandably, neither data set had much rural data for transit buses, and this is true even through their combination. Urban freeways on weekdays have moved from a point of caution to robust data through the addition of the two data sets. Additionally, urban freeway data on weekends can now be analyzed due to CE- CERT’s recorded hours (shaded yellow). For urban other roads on weekdays, FleetDNA already contained solid data (no shading) but has been augmented through combination.
